subject: design-technology
title: Basic Circuits
welcome_lead: Batteries, bulbs and the symbols engineers use.
meta_desc: KS3 D&T: simple circuits, series, parallel, symbols.
final_note: All electronics start with a circuit you can draw.

concepts.def: Single battery — one source of voltage.
Light Emitting Diode — current makes light.

walkthroughs.body_html: Electricity only flows in a closed circuit. Break the loop and it stops — that's all a switch does.
A simple circuit has a cell, switch, resistor and an LED or bulb. Each has a symbol you must learn for circuit diagrams.
In series, components are in one loop — if one fails all stop. In parallel, each is on its own branch — one can fail and others stay on. Christmas lights are parallel.

mcqs.q: What is FEA used for in product design?
options: Simulating how a product will respond to forces, heat, or vibration before manufacture.
Final exam analysis of student designs.
Counting the elements in a chemical compound.

mcqs.q: If voltage is doubled and resistance is unchanged, what happens to the current?
options: Counting the elements in a chemical compound.
Current doubles (V = IR, so I = V/R).
Producing a specific quantity of identical items, then switching to make another batch.
